# Memory, as the same `bytes` records a report uses - so an existing parser reads them
# without knowing this protocol exists.
CMD|1|hello|1
OBS|ack|1|hello
OBS|hello|1|5e6f7a8b|call,resolve,read,report
OBS|part|5e6f7a8b|target|console
OBS|part|5e6f7a8b|firmware|13.520.001
OBS|part|5e6f7a8b|probe|dev
OBS|done|1|ok||
# 0x20 bytes come back as two records of sixteen - the server caps a bytes record at 16
# bytes, and the offset field says where each chunk sits. Each hex run is a whole number of
# bytes (32 digits = 16 bytes); a run that is not is a defective record, and a consumer is
# right to refuse it rather than drop or invent a nibble.
CMD|2|read|0x8003f510|0x20
OBS|ack|2|read
OBS|bytes|read/0x8003f510|(memory)|contents|0|35000000610000000000000000000000
OBS|bytes|read/0x8003f510|(memory)|contents|16|37000000610000000c23000000000000
OBS|done|2|returned|0x20|
# An address this platform can test before touching. It answers `unmapped` rather than
# faulting - and that is a DIFFERENT fact from the death in 03-died.txt. "Not readable"
# and "asking killed the process" are both legitimate behaviours and the record says which.
CMD|3|read|0xdead0000|0x10
OBS|ack|3|read
OBS|refused|3|unmapped
CMD|4|bye
OBS|ack|4|bye
OBS|done|4|ok||
